================================================================================
             SYSADMIN PROTOCOLS // PROCESSES, MODES & NETWORKING
================================================================================
1. PROCESS SUPERVISION & SIGNALS:
   • 'ps aux'         : Inspect the active Process Status table (PID, %CPU, COMMAND).

2. PERMISSIONS & FILE MODES:
   • 'chmod +x <file>': Grant executable rights (r-x) to recovery scripts.
   • 'chmod 644 <file>': Lock down configuration files to read-only security.

3. NETWORKING & RECOVERY TOOLS:
   • 'ip link set <dev> up'      : Bring offline network interfaces to UP state.
   • 'ping <gateway>'            : Verify ICMP reachability to core gateway nodes.
   • 'find <path> -name "<pat>"'  : Scan partition trees for hidden keys.

HOW_TO_READ_LOGS.txt.content:
================================================================================
          APOLLO SECOPS FIELD MANUAL // HOW TO READ SYSTEM LOGS
================================================================================
Alice — when an attack happens, system daemons log events to /var/log/.
Raw logs look dense, but every line follows a strict 4-part anatomy:

  [ TIMESTAMP ]  [ HOST ]  [ DAEMON/SERVICE ]   [ EVENT MESSAGE ]
  03:38:10       apollo    sshd[204]:           Invalid user operator from 192.168.1.105
  └── When       └── Where └── Who logged it    └── What actually happened

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE 4 COMMON INCIDENT DAEMONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• 'sshd[PID]'   : Secure Shell logins (brute force attacks, unauthorized entry).
• 'sudo'        : Administrator privilege escalation.
• 'kernel'      : Core OS hardware & network link events.
• 'systemd[1]'  : System service supervisor (terminated daemons).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. YOUR LOG INVESTIGATION TOOLKIT:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• cat <file>            : Stream an entire log from start to finish.
• head -n 5 <file>      : Peek at the earliest events (e.g. system boot).
• tail -n 10 <file>     : Focus on the latest events (e.g. recent attack activity).
• grep -i "pattern" <file>: Filter the noise to isolate specific keywords or alerts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TRIAGE VERIFICATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Read 'REPAIR_COMMANDS.txt' for the list of triage verification commands to
register confirmed security leads into your incident dossier.
================================================================================

NOTE_FROM_MORGAN.txt.content:
// MORGAN [03:42 AM] — INCIDENT OVERRIDE
Alice — during the breach, your shell profile was wiped out, which broke your
command search paths and shortcuts.

I left a clean backup template right here ('alice.bashrc').

To clone it back into your home directory, write it over with '>':
  cat alice.bashrc > /home/alice/.bashrc

(Note: '~' is shorthand for your home folder, so 'cat alice.bashrc > ~/.bashrc' also works!)

Once restored, try typing 'll' right here.
The 'll' shortcut not only displays full file details (permissions, owner, size),
it also reveals secret hidden files and directories starting with a dot (.)!

[PRO TIP]: Restoring ~/.bashrc re-enables [TAB] autocompletion!
Type 'cd /o' and press [TAB] anywhere to autocomplete long paths instantly.

.HOW_TO_READ_LL.txt.content:
================================================================================
         SYSADMIN REFERENCE GUIDE // HOW TO READ 'll' (LONG LISTING)
================================================================================
Standard 'ls' only shows visible filenames.
The 'll' shortcut reveals hidden dotfiles and prints 5 critical columns:

  [ PERMISSIONS ]  [ LINKS ]  [ OWNER ]  [ SIZE ]  [ FILENAME ]
  -rw-r--r--       1          root       4096      alice.bashrc
  drwxr-xr-x       1          root       4096      profiles/
  ----------       1          root       4096      recovery.sh

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DECODING THE PERMISSIONS COLUMN:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• 1st character: 'd' = Directory (folder), '-' = Regular file.
• Next 3 chars : Owner permissions:
                 'r' = Read (can view contents with 'cat' or 'head')
                 'w' = Write (can edit or overwrite with '>')
                 'x' = Execute (can run programs or scripts like './tool')
                 '-' = Permission revoked / missing.

[KEY RECOVERY TAKEAWAY]:
If a tool has '---' instead of 'r-x' or 'rwx', it cannot run!
You can restore executable permissions on any file using 'chmod +x <filename>'.
================================================================================
